P01-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.8 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם … (WEB “But you, son of man, hear” (web:Ezek.2.8)) turns to the prophet with a ve'attah address, but the addressee does not change, since 2:7 already speaks to him, and 2:7 ends on the rebellion refrain כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.7), which is no close-role formula; the ve'attah onset is therefore unlicensed, and the pe recorded after oshb:Ezek.2.7 (single-witness) corroborates the break without licensing it. The scroll appears at 2:9, וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה (oshb:Ezek.2.9) (“behold, a hand was stretched out to me” (web:Ezek.2.9)), and its inscription is read at 2:10, אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'); the samekh recorded after 2:10 stands at the 2:10/3:1 seam and is disclosed as texture inside the row rather than a cut, since the eating that follows continues the same scroll scene: 3:1 reopens with a further 'he said to me,' אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את (oshb:Ezek.3.1) ('eat this scroll'), intra-row, and the WEB chapter numeral falling at 2:10/3:1 is disclosed only as texture, never as boundary evidence. Close: 3:3, וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (oshb:Ezek.3.3) ('it was in my mouth as sweet as honey'), with a pe recorded after it, before the address turns from the scroll to the audience's character at 3:4. That close rests on the report of the eating, which carries no close-role formula, while its far face 3:4 opens on a further 'he said to me' inside the vision; with the onset's ve'attah unlicensed and no close-role formula at the close, neither of the row's own near faces carries a licensed signal, which is why the row carries reduced confidence.
P01-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 2:10/3:1, where the WEB prints a chapter break and a samekh is recorded (single-witness). Rejected because 3:1's 'he said to me', a licensed onset inside the vision, renews the command to the same prophet within the one scroll scene the samekh only pauses, and its far face 2:10 ends on the scroll's inscription with no close-role formula; the chapter division is the translation's layout, and treating the WEB numeral as a boundary would read that layout as evidence of the Hebrew witness.
P01-003.device_notes: Samekh after 2:10 (single-witness) disclosed as intra-row texture: the eating (3:1-3:3) continues under the 'he said to me' at 3:1, so the mark is not read as a unit-cutting seam. A second 'he said to me' heads 3:3, a licensed onset at the 3:2/3:3 seam, weighed and not taken: its far face 3:2 reports the eating itself with no close-role formula, and 3:3 repeats the command to the same prophet and completes the eating that 3:1 began, so a cut would strand a one-verse remainder that is no complete unit. The WEB paragraph/chapter break at 2:10/3:1 is named nowhere as boundary evidence.

P01-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting after 5:13 or after 5:15, at 5:13/5:14 or 5:15/5:16, where the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences stand, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, also weighed here, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, which would set the sign-act 5:1-4 against the interpretation 5:5-17: it is where the sign-act command to the prophet ends and the oracle concerning Jerusalem begins. Its far face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 (single witness) and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it is neither an utterance-formula verse nor one of the verses of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its near face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But a messenger formula counts as a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither condition holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet the second condition by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.
P01-009.device_notes: 17-verse unit, the whole chapter, over the 7-10 verse target; disclosed as over the target rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is one of the 122 verses carrying the long messenger formula, and each carries it verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, and the reason is not any absence of coincidence. A messenger formula is a sub-onset when the addressee changes or when the verse before it ends on a close-role formula, and neither holds at the three formula verses: none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 carries an utterance formula or belongs to the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses); 5:5 carries no second person, and the person shifts at 5:7 (2mp) and 5:8 (2fs) address Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, which this row reads as no change of addressee; and a parashah mark by itself cannot license the cut. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark this witness sets at the seam where this unit begins.

P01-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula immediately after 7:4's recognition close, which a pe follows (single-witness) — כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.7.5) “The Lord Yahweh says: ‘A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.” (web:Ezek.7.5). Close: 7:9, the 2mp recognition-family close carrying an appended participle, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.7.9) “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, strike.” (web:Ezek.7.9); this recognition member also carries the doubled “My eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) refrain — MEASURED at 5 verses book-wide (5:11, 7:4, 7:9, 8:18, 9:10) by a consonantal-skeleton sweep of the phrase *lo tachos eini* over the pointed Hebrew witness, the WEB contracting the clause at every one of those verses except 7:4, which is why the quotation cites web:Ezek.7.4 — the same refrain the close at 7:4 already carries, so 7:9 closes a distinct short unit before the unmarked doom-poem reopens at 7:10 with no formula of its own.
P01-013.strongest_rejected_alternative: The single 7:5-7:27 row. Rejected because 7:9 supplies its own recognition-family close carrying the same doubled refrain that closes 7:4, so this unit is bounded by that refrain on both sides; 7:10 opens with no formula device of its own, which leaves the far face of this close empty but gives the doom-poem no claim to continue this unit.
P01-013.device_notes: Five-verse unit; justified by the fresh messenger-formula onset at 7:5 and the doubled-refrain recognition close at 7:9 (shared with 7:4), not by size. Disclosed as short, not capped. MEASURED in this witness (single-witness), which records a mark on the verse it follows: a pe is recorded on MT 7:4, so the witness breaks immediately before this row's first verse; inside the row, 7:5-7:8 carry no mark; and at the close no samekh and no pe is recorded on MT 7:9. The witness's own sectioning, read against this row: the next mark after the pe on MT 7:4 is the pe on MT 7:22, so the witness's own open section runs 7:5-7:22 and this row's close at 7:9 falls inside it. That sectioning corroborates the longer rival rather than this row, and it is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates. It does not unseat the row: a section boundary of the witness is weak corroboration that never outranks a licensed text signal, and the near face of this close carries one — the 2mp recognition clause at 7:9, whose only word after the formula is the dependent participle מַכֶּֽה (MEASURED: in the verse's consonantal skeleton, the clause quoted here in pointed form, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה occupies characters 63-80 of 84, counting from 1 with both ends included, with מַכֶּֽה filling the remainder), so it is verse-final in effect and grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The absence of a mark at 7:9 is disclosed and is never read as counter-evidence (oshb:Ezek.7.9).

P02-004.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut at 9:8/9:9. Its near face is licensed, 9:9 opening on וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.9.9), a 'he said to me' inside the vision; its far face is not, 9:8 ending on the prophet's outcry over the remnant of Israel with no formula and no mark. It is weighed and not taken, because 9:9 is the answer to that outcry within the same slaughter scene, which completes only when the man in linen reports his task done at 9:11, and a cut there would part the question from its answer. Splitting at oshb:Ezek.9.3, where the samekh sits (single-witness) and where the glory rises from the cherub to the threshold, was weighed as well (it would separate the mark-setting from the slaughter-command proper). It was not taken because the glory's rise at 9:3 is preparatory to the same command sequence that continues without any address or addressee change through 9:11, and the mid-row mark is disclosed rather than adopted as the cut.

P02-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.12.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula, opens the collection of undated oracles immediately after the vision report closes at 11:25; oshb:Ezek.12.2 names the addressee 'the rebellious house' (בית המרי), the disputation refrain that the commission narrative of chapters 2-3 also uses; the phrase, with or without the article, stands on 12 verses of this witness book-wide (MEASURED), six of them in chapters 2-3. MT 11:25 is followed by a pe (single witness), corroborating the onset of this unit at 12:1. Close: oshb:Ezek.12.7 וָאַ֣עַשׂ כֵּן֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּיתִי֒ כֵּ֠לַי הוֹצֵ֜אתִי כִּכְלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וּבָעֶ֛רֶב חָתַֽרְתִּי לִ֥י בַקִּ֖יר בְּיָ֑ד בָּעֲלָטָ֥ה הוֹצֵ֛אתִי עַל כָּתֵ֥ף נָשָׂ֖אתִי לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם — “I did so as I was commanded.” (web:Ezek.12.7) — reports the sign-act's execution, immediately before a fresh word-event at oshb:Ezek.12.8 reopens with an infixed 'in the morning' phrase. A pe follows oshb:Ezek.12.7 (single-witness). The onset seam is two-faced: 11:25 completes the vision's return, and 12:1 carries the strict word-event formula (sweep: 39 verses). The close seam is weaker on its near side: 12:7 reports the sign-act's execution with no close-role formula, the pe after it corroborating without licensing it, while its far face 12:8 carries the word-event formula with a phrase inserted into it (one of the two verses in the 41-verse vayehi-any word-event count whose formula an inserted phrase interrupts, here 'in the morning'). That execution report without a formula is the ground of the lower grade.
P02-011.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 12:1-16 as one sixteen-verse row (the sign-act and its full interpretation together) was weighed, since nothing but the 12:8 re-onset separates the command from the interpretation. It was not taken because 12:8 is itself a genuine word-event onset (its formula interrupted by 'in the morning', one of only two verses in the book whose word-event formula is interrupted by an inserted phrase) and a pe already corroborates the 12:7 stopping point, giving this split two independent anchors rather than the zero anchors a sixteen-verse row would rest the choice on.

P03-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 17:1 opens (oshb:Ezek.17.1) with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, and 17:2 names the genre directly, בֶּן אָדָ֕ם ח֥וּד חִידָ֖ה וּמְשֹׁ֣ל מָשָׁ֑ל אֶל בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.17.2) (rendered “Son of man, tell a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel”, web:Ezek.17.2), before the messenger formula כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.17.3) opens the eagle-and-vine figure itself. Close side: this row runs through 17:10, whose concluding clause תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ (oshb:Ezek.17.10) ('it will surely wither') answers the riddle's own rhetorical question, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse in the single-witness paragraph layer -- the riddle's content is complete and the mark coincides with it, so the row is closed here before the interpretation opens with its own word-event formula at 17:11. The onset seam is two-faced: 16:63 ends verse-final on the utterance formula, a samekh standing after it (single witness), against 17:1's strict word-event formula. The close seam is not: its near face 17:10 ends on the riddle's answer, a content close with no close-role formula that the pe there corroborates without licensing, though its far face 17:11 carries the same strict word-event formula; that formula-less close keeps the grade below medium.

P03-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:1 opens on the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.18.1); 18:2 quotes the popular proverb the oracle will refute, אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה (oshb:Ezek.18.2) (“The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”, web:Ezek.18.2). Close side: the span closes at 18:4, whose final clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.4) ('the soul who sins shall die') states the disputation's thesis, and a samekh stands on this same verse in the single witness. An oath formula with the utterance signature stands at the head of 18:3, in that verse's first five words ('as I live, declares the Lord YHWH'), weighed as texture inside the refutation rather than a row-final close, since the clause on the proverb's future use runs on after it to the end of the same verse. The close at 18:4/18:5 is a case turn inside one word-event unit: 18:4 ends on the disputation's thesis and carries a samekh, 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own, and the samekh corroborates that turn without deciding it. A close seam of that shape keeps a row under medium confidence, and this row is graded so. The onset seam, by contrast, is two-faced and top grade: 17:24 ends on the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula, verse-final, with a pe recorded after it, against 18:1's strict word-event formula.
P03-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 18:9 (thesis plus the first case-law example together) was weighed and not taken: the samekh on 18:4 (single witness) corroborates a close for the thesis statement alone without deciding it, and 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own -- a fresh case argued on its own terms, rather than an illustration folded into the thesis that precedes it.

P03-021.boundary_rationale: Onset: 18:21 opens the case of the wicked man who turns, וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ (oshb:Ezek.18.21) (“But if the wicked turns from all his sins” (web:Ezek.18.21)), with no onset-class device of its own; its far face 18:20 closes the preceding case on the principle that a person's own righteousness or wickedness rests on that person, and ends on no close-role formula, the samekh after it (single-witness) corroborating the break only. Close: 18:32 carries the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.32) mid-verse, and the independent imperative וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ (oshb:Ezek.18.32) follows it, “Therefore turn yourselves, and live!” (web:Ezek.18.32), so the formula does not stand at the verse's end; a pe follows the verse, and the far face 19:1 opens on the command to take up a lament, וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.19.1). Between these seams the span argues one case: the wicked man who turns (18:21-23), the righteous man who turns away (18:24), the people's objection, the two cases restated and the objection repeated (18:25-29), and the closing appeal (18:30-32). The utterance formula standing mid-verse in 18:23 with a samekh after it, the samekh after 18:26, and the therefore-turn at 18:30 mark paragraphs inside that one appeal, and none of them carries a licensed onset. Neither of the row's own near faces carries a licensed signal, since the onset opens with no formula and the close's formula stands mid-verse, and only the far face of the close, 19:1, is licensed; the row is held at reduced confidence on those faces.
P03-021.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 18:23/18:24 was weighed and not taken. Its far face is the strongest side of any seam inside the span: 18:23 carries the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.23) mid-verse, followed by the independent question הֲל֛וֹא בְּשׁוּב֥וֹ מִדְּרָכָ֖יו וְחָיָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.23), and a samekh stands after the verse (single-witness). Its near face carries nothing: 18:24 opens the reverse case of the righteous man who turns away with no onset-class device. A mid-verse formula makes no close, and a mark alone licenses no cut, so the seam is a paragraph turn from one case to its mirror inside the one appeal.

P08-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: MT 33:20 is followed by a pe (single-witness), corroborating the onset at 33:21; that pe stands where this witness records no sof pasuq on MT 33:20, and it is the only corroboration the onset carries from behind. The dateline at Ezek.33.21 וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר (oshb:Ezek.33.21) — one of the book's 14 year-bearing oracle datelines and a hard seam — reports the fugitive's arrival with news the city has fallen. Ezek.33.22 וְיַד יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בָּעֶ֗רֶב לִפְנֵי֙ בּ֣וֹא הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח אֶת פִּ֔י עַד בּ֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּפָּ֣תַח פִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱלַ֖מְתִּי עֽוֹד (oshb:Ezek.33.22) follows with the hand-of-YHWH idiom (matched on the construct alone, one of 7 verses carrying the construct) and the mouth-opening event that fulfils the muteness first commissioned in ch. 3 and anticipated as a coming sign earlier in the book. This hand-of-YHWH occurrence opens no vision here — it is narrative notice, not a scene-transport marker. Close: a pe mark follows Ezek.33.22 (single-witness), and the verse completes the narrative beat before Ezek.33.23 opens a fresh, formally distinct word-event oracle. The onset's near face is licensed -- the dateline itself -- while the far face behind it carries that mark and no formula; the close's near face is weaker, since 33:22 reports the hand of YHWH and the opening of the prophet's mouth as narrative notice and carries no close-role signal, though its far face is 33:23's fresh word-event formula. That close, not the licensed onset, is the ground for the reduced grade this row carries.
P08-003.device_notes: The unit is classed as a commission narrative, a choice made on the bytes and disclosed as a departure (the muteness/mouth-opening device), rather than as a vision report, because the hand-of-YHWH here is followed by narrative notice (the mouth-opening at Ezek.33.22) rather than any scene-transport or vision-inaugurating formula, and rather than as a disputation or judgment oracle because the verses are narrative notice, not oracle speech. Under-3-verse row, disclosed as a two-verse unit bounded by 33:21's own dateline onset and the pe after 33:22 (single-witness).

P08-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: the sub-onset “As for you, son of man,” (web:Ezek.33.30) at Ezek.33.30 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ הַנִּדְבָּרִ֤ים בְּךָ֙ אֵ֣צֶל הַקִּיר֔וֹת וּבְפִתְחֵ֖י הַבָּתִּ֑ים וְדִבֶּר חַ֣ד אֶת אַחַ֗ד אִ֤ישׁ אֶת אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֹּֽאוּ נָ֣א וְשִׁמְע֔וּ מָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר הַיּוֹצֵ֖א מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.30) opens a new complaint about the people's reception of the prophet, distinct from the land-inheritance dispute just closed. Close: the chapter's final verse, Ezek.33.33 וּבְבֹאָ֑הּ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י נָבִ֖יא הָיָ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.33.33), states the outcome (“then they will know that a prophet has been among them” (web:Ezek.33.33)) in a clause that functions like a recognition close but does not match the standard 'know that I am Yahweh' formula bytes; it is disclosed here as a non-formulaic close rather than claimed as formula-count membership. A samekh mark follows Ezek.33.33 (single-witness), corroborating the chapter's own end, immediately before Ezek.34.1's fresh word-event (hard seam). The onset seam is licensed on both faces, 33:29 ending on its recognition formula, verse-final in effect, with a samekh after it, before 33:30's address to the son of man; the close is weaker, because a recognition-shaped clause that the counted recognition classes do not include makes a weak near face however strong the word-event beyond it, and that near face grounds the lower grade.
P08-005.device_notes: The disputation-oracle category fits 33.30-33 as one unit, with no departure from that category. Close is explicitly flagged as non-formulaic so as not to inflate any of the book's recognition-formula counts.

P09-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: a messenger formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.39.25 לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה עַתָּ֗ה אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת שבית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְקִנֵּאתִ֖י לְשֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי on the word ‘therefore,’ immediately turning from the exile retrospective to the restoration promise. That turn addresses the same hearers as the retrospective before it, so it is a discourse turn and not a licensed sub-onset, and the far face behind it, oshb:Ezek.39.24, carries a samekh (single-witness) and no close-role formula -- its hidden-face clause is not a close device -- so the onset seam is corroborated by a mark alone. In 39.25 the ketiv reads שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv) and the qere reads שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere) (a single-witness textual-variant site, disclosed, never argued as a boundary). Close: 39.25-29 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.29 וְלֹֽא אַסְתִּ֥יר ע֛וֹד פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁפַ֤כְתִּי אֶת רוּחִי֙ עַל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה, the standard utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (one of 81 book-wide) with a pe mark recorded immediately after -- the close evidence the restoration collection's own boundary is anchored on, matching the point where the following material opens on a dateline plus hand-of-YHWH and transport at Ezek.40.1. The close seam stands top grade on both faces -- 39.29's utterance signature with the pe recorded after it, and the dateline with hand-of-YHWH and transport at 40.1 past it -- while the onset seam's near face is a therefore-turn messenger formula that neither a change of addressee nor a verse-final close licenses, and that unlicensed near face is what grounds this row's reduced confidence.
P09-011.device_notes: No paseq falls in this span. MT 39:25 is a single-note K/Q verse (written שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv), read שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere)); no editorial note falls here. The span closes at 39:29, the restoration collection's own close; no material past 39:29 is claimed. The strict recognition formula stands at 39:28, interior to the span and not its close. The hidden-face clause that ends 39:24 recurs, negated, at 39:29, straddling this row's onset seam; it argues continuity across the seam and is disclosed as such.

P10-004.device_notes: No parashah mark touches ch 40 at all. Four of the book's twenty-three doubled-note K/Q verses fall inside this row (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26), plus a single note at 40:25; every one checked here is the recurring defective/plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on architectural nouns (chambers, posts, porches, windows, palm-trees), never on the cubit figures. P10-012.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1, a verse of the counted transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', beginning a hard seam as the transport leads the prophet from the completed measuring circuit to the gate, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and the prostration “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3), one of five verses where the WEB reads “I fell on my face” (sweep: 5 verses). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This close is the first since the pe at 39:29 to carry a parashah mark, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so. Its near face is the resolution clause itself, which answers the dwelling promise of 43:7, אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶשְׁכָּן שָׁ֛ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעוֹלָ֑ם (oshb:Ezek.43.7), as an inclusio but carries no close-role formula; with the transport onset at 43:1 licensed and the two licensed onsets inside the span held on the grounds weighed below, that formula-less close is the ground of the row's reduced confidence.
P10-012.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut at 43:6/43:7, which would set the glory's return against the throne speech, six verses before the seam and three after it. Its near face is licensed: 43:7 opens on וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.43.7), a 'he said to me' inside the vision. Its far face carries no device: 43:6's “I heard one speaking to me out of the house” (web:Ezek.43.6) introduces the same speaker whose words 43:7 begins, and no mark stands after it. The cut was weighed and rejected, because the throne declaration at 43:7 is the content the glory's return was staged to deliver and the voice heard at 43:6 already binds that speech to the scene.
P10-012.device_notes: The samekh at 43:9 is single-witness Masoretic paragraph evidence, disclosed and treated as corroboration only, never as the sole ground for the seam (the hard-seam onset at 43:1 and the resolution clause at 43:9 stand independently of it). No K/Q or editorial note touches 43:1-43:9. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: one occurrence, at 43:8, inside the defilement polemic. A cut at 43:4/43:5 is weighed and not taken: 43:5's transport, וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ וַתְּבִיאֵ֕נִי (oshb:Ezek.43.5), is a licensed onset inside the vision, but its far face 43:4 ends on the glory's entry by the east gate with no formula or mark, and the transport only carries the prophet into the inner court to see that same glory fill the house, so a four-and-five tiling would divide one arrival. Content note: vv 7-9 carry polemic close to temple law (royal defilement) inside a row classed as a vision report because the glory-return frame and the throne-declaration speech dominate it.

P11-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.45.18, following the samekh recorded after Ezek.45.17 (single-witness), opens this row; the law paragraph before it (45.9-17) ends at that samekh on the prince's offerings with no close-role formula, and the hearers do not change, so the formula is not a licensed sub-onset. The samekh corroborates the break, and the seam is kept as a paragraph-grade seam because the book's division of the temple law sets the festival calendar apart as its own law paragraph. Ezek.45.18 also carries a full month+day date construction in the same verse, but the date clause carries no year word, so it fails the book's structural dateline test (a YEAR word together with a month or day term) and is disclosed as NOT a dateline and NOT onset evidence in its own right; it is one of exactly four calendar dates in the book (45.18, 45.20, 45.21, 45.25) that carry a month/day construction without a year, and none of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines falls anywhere across 44.1-48.35. The unit that follows is the single festival-calendar paragraph running 45.18-25: New Year sanctuary cleansing (18-20, itself containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.20), Passover (21-24, containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.21), and the seventh-month feast (25, containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.25). Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.45.25 closes both the calendar-law paragraph and the chapter.

P11-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.46.16 opens a fresh legal topic -- the prince's inheritance rules -- directly after the pe recorded after Ezek.46.15 (single-witness), on a distinct subject (inheritance, not the cultic calendar) from the cultic-calendar law before it (46.1-15). A change of topic licenses nothing: the hearers do not change, and 46:15 ends on the daily burnt offering with no close-role formula, so the formula is not a licensed sub-onset; the open-section mark corroborates the break, and the seam is paragraph-grade, kept because the book's division sets the prince's inheritance law apart as its own paragraph within the chapter. The row's reduced confidence rests on that onset. The row covers the prince's gift to a son (16), to a servant (17, carrying 'the year of liberty', a year word that is NOT a dateline), and the prohibition on seizing the people's inheritance (18). Close: no parashah mark is recorded on 46.16, 46.17 or 46.18. This row's close is argued instead from the adjacent hard seam at 46.18/46.19, where a transport verb reopens a vision scene -- a shift from temple law to vision report -- a text-signalled close, the samekh recorded after Ezek.46.19 standing beyond the row. The close holds although the row's own last verse carries no parashah mark.
P11-008.device_notes: Ezek.46.17 carries 'the year of liberty', a year word explicitly NOT a dateline, disclosed. This row's close at 46.18/46.19 is a hard seam (a shift from temple law to vision report) rather than a parashah-marked close; the samekh recorded after Ezek.46.19 is disclosed at that verse, not here.
